problem:
Consider the transformation $T:(u,v)\to (x(u,v),y(u,v)).$ The inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}(x,y)\to (u(x,y),v(x,y))$ is given by

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}2x-y \\ x+2y\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the Jacobian determinant of $T.$

examples.problem:
Consider all non-critical points of the transformation $\mathbf{T}:(u,v) \to (x(u,v),y(u,v)).$ The inverse transformation $\mathbf T^{-1}(x,y)\to(u(x,y), v(x,y))$ is given by

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14044887/assets/2614cbd879ea1014caf69d1239b69e81ebefcc76b8946962092cb83cc96dc987.png)

Find the Jacobian determinant of $\mathbf T$ in terms of $u$ and $v.$
examples.worked_solution:
Given a transformation 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14044887/assets/149438cd70059230993ca93a2122158f71edb665b3948cbd4ff3a9c038d7e48f.png)

the Jacobian determinant of $\mathbf T,$ denoted $\dfrac{\partial (x, y)}{\partial (u, v)} ,$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, we're only given $\mathbf T^{-1}.$ So, we compute the Jacobian determinant of $\mathbf T$ as follows:

- First, we compute $\dfrac{\partial (u, v)}{\partial (x, y)},$ the Jacobian determinant of $\mathbf T^{-1}.$

- Then, we will compute the Jacobian determinant of $\mathbf T$ using the relation

$$
\dfrac{\partial (x, y)}{\partial (u, v)} = \left( \dfrac{\partial (u, v)}{\partial (x, y)} \right)^{-1}.
$$

Here, we have $u(x,y) = e^{x+y}$ and $v(x,y) = e^{x-y}.$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & ={e}^{x+y} & \,\frac{∂u}{∂y} & ={e}^{x+y} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & ={e}^{x-y} & \,\frac{∂v}{∂y} & =-{e}^{x-y}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}{e}^{x+y} & {e}^{x+y} \\ {e}^{x-y} & -{e}^{x-y}\end{aligned}| \\  & ={e}^{x+y}\cdot (-{e}^{x-y})-{e}^{x+y}\cdot {e}^{x-y} \\  & =-{e}^{x+y}\cdot {e}^{x-y}-{e}^{x+y}\cdot {e}^{x-y} \\  & =-2\cdot {e}^{x+y}\cdot {e}^{x-y} \\  & =-2uv.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we take the reciprocal:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & ={(\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)})}^{-1} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2uv}\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Find the locations of all of the critical points of $T,$ where $T$ is defined as

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}uv \\ u+v\end{aligned}].
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v) \\ y(u,v)\end{aligned}],
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the locations of the critical points of $T,$ we need to solve 

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}=0.
$$

Here, we have $x(u,v)=uv$ and $y(u,v)=u+v.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =v & \,\frac{∂x}{∂v} & =u \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =1 & \,\frac{∂y}{∂v} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}v & u \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =v\cdot 1-u\cdot 1 \\  & =v-u.\end{aligned}
$$

The function has critical points when $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}=0.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =0 \\ v-u & =0 \\ v & =u.\end{aligned}
$$

The equation $v=u$ defines a line in the $uv$-plane.

submitted_fields.submitted_value: The critical points lie on the line $v=u.$
